function.name: give_up
function.arguments: {"reason": "Move execution is throttled: the first move_to ran 39 steps, every subsequent one ran 1-4 steps (about 2-4mm of end-effector travel) regardless of commanded distance, target size, gripper latching, or near-rest joint velocities, and the robot state freezes between calls. I localized the red block near x=-0.105, y=0.068 and descended from z=1.02 to z=0.904, but about 4cm of approach remained just to reach grasp height, followed by closing, lifting, and transporting roughly 15cm to the blue bowl. At the observed 2-4mm per policy call this needs far more than my 8 remaining decisions, so completion within budget is impossible.", "hindsight": "On this rig the move_to interpolation is truncated to 1-4 control steps (2-4mm) per policy call after the very first action, so a whole pick-and-place cannot fit in a 20-call budget; do not spend calls on calibration probes since every move only creeps. The wrist camera image places the table scene with the bowl at image top and the red block right of the fingertip gap; the block being right of the gap corresponded to the block sitting at larger world y, which agreed with the fixed front camera where the block appeared right of the gripper. The fixed side camera reads world x directly: gripper and block were x-aligned within a few pixels all trial. Fingertips sit roughly 6cm below the reported eef_pos: at eef z=0.905 the fingertips were already at block-top height (block top around z=0.845, table at 0.80). Closing on the block likely needs eef z around 0.87-0.88. The 900-step episode budget is not the binding constraint - the per-call truncation is."}
